learn.title: Two ideas to start
learn.body: Every circuit is built on two ideas. Voltage is the push that moves charge. Current is the flow of charge that results. A battery gives the push, and wires give the path.

learn.title: Voltage
learn.body: Voltage is measured in volts (V). It is the push between two points, such as the two ends of a battery. A typical AA battery gives about 1.5 V. You always measure voltage across two points.

learn.title: Current
learn.body: Current is how much charge passes a point each second. It is measured in amperes (A), also called amps. $I=\frac{Q}{t}$ where $Q$ is charge in coulombs and $t$ is time in seconds.

learn.title: Find the current
learn.body: 12 coulombs of charge pass a point in 4 seconds.

learn.title: Small currents
learn.body: Many electronics use small currents, measured in milliamps (mA). $1\ \text{A}=1000\ \text{mA}$. So $250\ \text{mA}=0.25\ \text{A}$. To go from mA to A, divide by 1000.
Voltage is measured across two points. Current flows through a path.

questions.explanation: Current is measured in amperes. Volts measure voltage.

questions.prompt: 10 C of charge pass in 5 s. What is the current in A?
Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: The battery pushes, the wire carries, and the flow is the current.

questions.prompt: $I=\frac{Q}{t}$ means current is charge divided by \_\_.
questions.explanation: Current is charge per second, so you divide by time.

questions.prompt: An AA battery is rated 1.5 V. What does that number describe?
questions.explanation: Volts measure the push, not the flow.
